message.content:
Below are two ways to launch a **Google Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA GPU and boots from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If you’re looking for an “EC2”‑style instance, that’s Amazon Web Services – Google calls its equivalent “Compute Engine”.)

> **Important:**  
> Google Cloud does **not** offer an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU.  
> The closest GPU types available are the NVIDIA A100, A40, A30, A10, etc.  
> If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to use another provider (e.g., AWS, Azure) or wait until Google adds it to their catalog.

---

## 1. Using `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Replace placeholders:
#   PROJECT_ID   – your GCP project id
#   ZONE         – e.g., us-central1-a
#   INSTANCE     – desired instance name
#   MACHINE_TYPE – e.g., n1-highmem-8 (or any supported type)
#   GPU_COUNT    – number of GPUs (max 8 per instance)

gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=$MACHINE_TYPE \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a100,count=1 \   # <-- change to the GPU you actually need
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: script to install drivers
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--project` | Your GCP project ID |
| `--zone` | Compute Engine zone (e.g., `us-central1-a`) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/memory configuration (e.g., `n1-highmem-8`) |
| `--accelerator` | Attach a GPU (`type=nvidia-a100`, `count=1`) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boot from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | Persistent Disk type (`pd-standard` or `pd-ssd`) |
| `--maintenance-policy` | How to handle maintenance events (`MIGRATE` keeps the VM running) |
| `--scopes` | Permissions for the instance (full cloud platform access) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script to run at first boot (useful for installing NVIDIA drivers) |

> **Tip:** After the instance starts, you’ll still need to install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit manually (unless you use a custom image that already contains them).

---

## 2. Using the Compute Engine REST API

Below is a minimal JSON payload you would POST to the Compute Engine API endpoint.  
Make sure you have OAuth 2.0 credentials with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.

```json
{
  "name": "my-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/types/nvidia-a100"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Making the API Call

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace:

* `my-project` → your GCP project ID
* `us-central1-a` → your desired zone
* `my-instance` → your desired instance name
* `nvidia-a100` → the GPU type you actually need

---

## Next Steps

1. **Enable the Compute Engine API** in your project (via the Cloud Console or `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).
2. **Create a service account** with the necessary permissions if you’re using the REST API.
3. **Install NVIDIA drivers** on the instance after it boots (you can automate this via a startup script or use a custom image that already includes them).

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help writing a startup script to automatically install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit!
